sources.license: Public domain in the USA; see source edition and local copyright law.

sources.license: Public domain in the USA; see source edition and local copyright law.

sources.license: Public domain in the USA; see source edition and local copyright law.

sources.license: Public domain in the USA; see source edition and local copyright law.

sources.title: Islâm
sources.author: Syed Ameer Ali
sources.license: Public domain in the USA; see source edition and local copyright law.
sources.coverageNotes: An author's historical apologetic presentation, not a comprehensive statement of Sunni or Shi'a doctrine.

sources.title: The Meaning of the Glorious Koran — Pickthall translation
sources.author: Qur'an; English interpretation by Marmaduke Pickthall
sources.license: Public domain in the USA; see source edition and local copyright law.
sources.coverageNotes: Only the Pickthall text is extracted from the three-translation source. English interpretation is not the Arabic Qur'an. Four malformed source locators are normalized using their chapter and sequential position: 0.033→17:33, 039.04→39:46, 04.032→45:32, 05.026→56:26; wording is unchanged.

sources.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox, Catholic, Eastern Church
sources.author: Philaret of Moscow
sources.translator: R. W. Blackmore; Philip Schaff, editor
sources.license: Public domain in the USA; see source edition and local copyright law.
sources.coverageNotes: Complete catechism excerpted from Schaff's collection, excluding his introductory evaluation. A historical Russian Orthodox source, not every Orthodox jurisdiction.

completeness: Historical starting collection, not exhaustive or statistically representative.
gaps: Contemporary scholarship and modern translations require additional permissions.
Anglican, Anabaptist, Pentecostal, Oriental Orthodox and many other Christian voices are not yet sampled.
Jewish Conservative, Reconstructionist, Hasidic and contemporary Orthodox voices are not adequately represented.
Shi'a, Ibadi and contemporary Sunni schools are not adequately represented; a modernist author is not a substitute for them.
English translations predominate. Translation and editor voices must be distinguished from original authors.
No quantity of downloaded text establishes doctrinal truth or consensus.
attributionPolicy: Identify the author and historical perspective; distinguish assertion, quotation, objection, reply and editorial survey. Do not infer group consensus from one author.
trainingStatus: Downloaded and segmented; no custom language-model weights trained.
